newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS POUND FLYERS TO TAKE 3-0 STANLEY CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS POUND FLYERS TO TAKE 3-0 STANLEY CUP LEAD.

text.p: Sergei Fedorov scored twice and assisted on a pair of goals by Martin Lapointe as the high-flying Detroit Red Wings embarrassed the Philadelphia Flyers 6-1 Thursday to move within one victory of their first Stanley Cup since 1955.

Steve Yzerman and Brendan Shanahan also scored for Detroit, which holds a commanding three games to none lead in the best-of-seven National Hockey League championship series after again outplaying the Flyers in every phase of the game.
The Red Wings can end the longest current title drought in the NHL and complete a sweep of the Flyers with a victory at home on Saturday.

The Flyers, playing without veteran defenceman Paul Coffey who stayed home with a consussion, again suffered from numerous mistakes, defensive lapses and poor goaltending, despite switching back to veteran Ron Hextall in goal after a shaky Game 2 performance by Garth Snow.
Philadelphia now faces the daunting task of trying to come back from a 3-0 finals deficit, something that was accomplished just once before by the 1942 Toronto Maple Leafs.

But with Detroit firing on all cylindars at home in the motor city and seemingly capitalising on every Philadelphia mistake -- of which there have been no shortage -- the Flyers would do well simply to avoid a sweep.
"We've got to find a way to stop the bleeding," said stunned Philadelphia coach Terry Murray, whose team dominated every opponent in the previous three rounds.
"There's no doubt that the game today was an embarrassment. Detroit came out and really took it to us."
Detroit also got two assists from Vyacheslav Kozlov and one from Viacheslav Fetisov, improving to 15-0 in the playoffs when a member of its "Russian Five" records at least a point.

Detroit goaltender Mike Vernon, allowing an average of less than two goals a game in the playoffs, made 21 stops and was rarely called upon to make a big save after giving up a goal to John LeClair in the first period.
Hextall, forced into big save situations throughout by his team's poor defensive play, made precious few of them.
LeClair's powerplay goal 7:03 into the contest gave the Flyers their first lead of the series. But it was short-lived.
Wings captain Yzerman tied the game exactly two minutes later with a powerplay goal and two minutes after that Fedorov put Detroit ahead to stay.
The lightning-fast Russian centre took the puck right off the stick of Flyers defenceman Karl Dykhuis, broke in alone and easily snapped the puck past Hextall for a 2-1 lead.
Philadelphia had a golden opportunity to get back into it with a two-man advantage that lasted 80 seconds.
But a powerplay that had struck fear in the hearts of most NHL teams this year was rendered impotent by Detroit's superior speed and sensational defensive play.

With a minute left in the period, LaPointe took a pass from Doug Brown, who was behind the Flyers net, and banged it in from the slot for his first goal of the finals, leaving Philadelphia 3-1 down at the first intermission.
Murray said he thought his team's fortunes had changed when they struck for the first goal of the game.
"(But) they came right back and gained the lead almost at will," he said with dismay.
Things didn't get any better for Philadelphia in the second period with Fedorov picking up his second goal of the game and eighth of the playoffs on a powerplay just 3:21 in.
The score remained 4-1 until the final minute of the period when Shanahan scored his third goal of the last two games.

This time Hextall appeared to make a big save off a shot by Darren McCarty. But nothing was going right for the Flyers as Shanahan retrieved the puck behind the net and banked it into the Flyers goal off the sprawled goaltender.

The long-suffering Red Wings fans started chanting, "sweep, sweep, sweep," after Lapointe scored his second of the game and Detroit's third powerplay goal of the night just 68 seconds into the final period to complete the scoring.

The Red Wings, who were swept out of the finals in 1995 and stunned in the semifinals last year after posting the best regular-season record ever in the NHL, are now just 60 minutes away from hoisting hockey's Holy Grail.
"It's going to be unbelievable for us and all the people of Detroit," Fedorov said.
